content.value_statement: WebSocket frame errors are hard to trace because HTTP upgrade conflicts can look like corrupted frames. This skill guides diagnosis of RSV1, invalid header, and code 1006 issues in Node.js ws servers.
actual_capabilities: Explains why multiple WebSocketServer instances can corrupt upgraded sockets.
Maps common WebSocket symptoms to likely causes and fixes.
Shows a noServer routing pattern for shared HTTP servers.
Provides raw frame inspection steps for Node.js ws clients.
Lists verification checks for RSV1 and extension negotiation.
limitations: It focuses on Node.js ws behavior, not browser WebSocket internals.
It does not inspect a running service without user-provided logs or code.
It does not replace protocol analysis tools for encrypted production traffic.
It assumes the developer can change server upgrade handling.

use_cases.title: Fix Invalid Frame Header Errors
use_cases.description: Diagnose why a WebSocket connects, then fails with invalid frame header or RSV1 errors.

use_cases.title: Route Shared WebSocket Upgrades
use_cases.description: Plan a single HTTP upgrade handler for multiple realtime endpoints on one server.

use_cases.title: Triage Production Disconnects
use_cases.description: Use logs, close codes, and frame clues to narrow code 1006 failures quickly.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a WebSocket Error
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner diagnosis from an error message.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me understand this WebSocket error: [paste error]. Ask for any logs you need, then map it to likely causes.

prompt_templates.title: Review Upgrade Routing
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this WebSocket server setup for upgrade handler conflicts: [paste code]. Identify whether noServer routing is needed.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Raw Frame Evidence
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced diagnosis using byte and log evidence.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these raw frame bytes and client logs: [paste data]. Explain whether the issue is raw HTTP, compression, or another frame problem.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Verification Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced validation after a server change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a verification plan after changing my ws server to noServer routing. Include checks for RSV1, extensions, and abnormal closures.

output_examples.input: A client reports WS_ERR_UNEXPECTED_RSV_1 after adding a second WebSocket endpoint.
output_examples.output: The likely cause is duplicate upgrade handling on the shared HTTP server. The response recommends one upgrade listener with explicit routing.

output_examples.input: Raw frame inspection shows the first bytes decode as HTTP.
output_examples.output: The output identifies HTTP text being written after upgrade. It points to a rejected handler or abort path writing to the socket.

output_examples.input: A service disconnects with code 1006 and no close reason.
output_examples.output: The guidance checks server-side aborts, compression negotiation, and competing listeners before deeper packet analysis.

best_practices: Route all upgrades through one handler when multiple ws servers share an HTTP server.
Disable or verify permessage-deflate when investigating RSV1 errors.
Capture raw frame headers and upgrade response headers before changing multiple variables.
anti_patterns: Creating multiple WebSocketServer instances with the server option on the same HTTP server.
Assuming every RSV1 error is a compression bug without checking for raw HTTP bytes.
Debugging code 1006 only from the browser console without server upgrade logs.

faq.question: What errors is this skill best for?
faq.answer: It is best for invalid frame header, RSV1 must be clear, WS_ERR_UNEXPECTED_RSV_1, and code 1006 symptoms.

faq.question: Does the skill run commands or network scans?
faq.answer: No. It provides diagnostic reasoning and code patterns for WebSocket server troubleshooting.

faq.question: Can it help with the ws npm package?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance focuses on Node.js ws servers and WebSocketServer upgrade handling.

faq.question: Why does noServer routing help?
faq.answer: It keeps one upgrade listener in control, so unmatched handlers do not write HTTP errors to upgraded sockets.

faq.question: Does it cover compression issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how RSV1 relates to permessage-deflate and when to verify extension negotiation.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the error text, server upgrade code, close code, frame bytes, and WebSocket extension headers.
